problems.title: Sum Two Numbers
problems.prompt: Write a function `add(a, b)` that returns the sum of `a` and `b`.
problems.hint: Add the two parameters together and return the result — you don't need any conditionals for this one.

problems.title: Even or Odd
problems.prompt: Write a function `is_even(n)` that returns `True` if `n` is even, and `False` otherwise.
problems.hint: A number is even if dividing it by 2 leaves no remainder. Try the modulo operator `%`.

problems.title: Max of Two
problems.prompt: Write a function `max_of_two(a, b)` that returns the larger of the two numbers. Do not use the built-in `max()` function.
problems.hint: Compare `a` and `b` with an if/else — return whichever one is bigger.

problems.title: Celsius to Fahrenheit
problems.prompt: Write a function `celsius_to_fahrenheit(c)` that converts a Celsius temperature to Fahrenheit using the formula `F = C * 9/5 + 32`. Return the result.
problems.hint: Plug `c` straight into the formula and return it. Watch your order of operations: multiply and divide before adding 32.

problems.title: String Repeat
problems.prompt: Write a function `repeat_string(s, n)` that returns the string `s` repeated `n` times.
problems.hint: Python strings support the `*` operator for repetition — try `s * n`.

problems.title: Reverse a String
problems.prompt: Write a function `reverse_string(s)` that returns `s` reversed.
problems.hint: Slicing with a step of -1 (`s[::-1]`) reverses a string in one line.

problems.title: Count Vowels
problems.prompt: Write a function `count_vowels(s)` that returns the number of vowels (`a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, `u` — lowercase only) in `s`.
problems.hint: Loop through each character in `s` and check if it's in the string `'aeiou'`.

problems.title: FizzBuzz (Single Number)
problems.prompt: Write a function `fizzbuzz(n)` that returns `"Fizz"` if `n` is divisible by 3, `"Buzz"` if divisible by 5, `"FizzBuzz"` if divisible by both, or `str(n)` otherwise.
problems.hint: Check the FizzBuzz cases in this order: divisible by both 3 and 5 first, then 3, then 5 — otherwise return `str(n)`.

problems.title: Is Palindrome
problems.prompt: Write a function `is_palindrome(s)` that returns `True` if `s` reads the same forwards and backwards, and `False` otherwise.
problems.hint: Compare `s` to its reverse (`s[::-1]`) — if they're equal, it's a palindrome.

problems.title: Grade Converter
problems.prompt: Write a function `letter_grade(score)` that returns `"A"` for 90+, `"B"` for 80-89, `"C"` for 70-79, `"D"` for 60-69, and `"F"` below 60.
problems.hint: Use if/elif/else and check the highest grade boundary first (90+), working your way down.

problems.title: Sum of a List
problems.prompt: Write a function `sum_list(nums)` that returns the sum of all numbers in the list `nums` using a loop (don't use the built-in `sum()`).
problems.hint: Start a `total` variable at 0, then loop through `nums` adding each value to it.

problems.title: Find the Maximum
problems.prompt: Write a function `find_max(nums)` that returns the largest number in the list `nums`, without using the built-in `max()`. Assume the list has at least one item.
problems.hint: Start by assuming the first item is the largest, then loop through the rest and update your answer whenever you find something bigger.

problems.title: Count Occurrences
problems.prompt: Write a function `count_occurrences(lst, target)` that returns how many times `target` appears in `lst`.
problems.hint: Start a counter at 0 and loop through `lst`, adding 1 every time you see `target`.

problems.title: Factorial
problems.prompt: Write a function `factorial(n)` that returns `n!` (the product of all integers from 1 to `n`). `factorial(0)` should return `1`.
problems.hint: Multiply numbers from 1 up to `n` together in a loop, starting your running product at 1 (not 0!).

problems.title: Fibonacci Number
problems.prompt: Write a function `fibonacci(n)` that returns the `n`th number in the Fibonacci sequence (0-indexed: `fibonacci(0) = 0`, `fibonacci(1) = 1`).
problems.hint: Keep track of the two most recent Fibonacci numbers and update them together each loop iteration.

problems.title: Filter Evens
problems.prompt: Write a function `filter_evens(nums)` that returns a new list containing only the even numbers from `nums`, in the same order.
problems.hint: Loop through `nums`, and use `.append()` to add a number to a new list only if it's even.

problems.title: Word Frequency
problems.prompt: Write a function `word_count(s)` that returns a dictionary mapping each word in `s` (split by spaces) to how many times it appears.
problems.hint: Split `s` into words with `.split()`, then loop through them, using a dictionary to count how many times you've seen each one.

testCases.call: word_count('the cat sat on the mat')

problems.title: Prime Checker
problems.prompt: Write a function `is_prime(n)` that returns `True` if `n` is a prime number (greater than 1, only divisible by 1 and itself), and `False` otherwise.
problems.hint: A number is prime if nothing between 2 and n-1 divides it evenly. Don't forget numbers less than 2 aren't prime!

problems.title: Remove Duplicates
problems.prompt: Write a function `remove_duplicates(lst)` that returns a new list with duplicate values removed, keeping only the first occurrence of each value (preserve order).
problems.hint: Loop through `lst` and build a new list, only adding a value if it isn't already in your new list.

problems.title: Caesar Cipher
problems.prompt: Write a function `caesar_encrypt(s, shift)` that shifts each lowercase letter in `s` forward by `shift` positions in the alphabet, wrapping around from `z` back to `a`. Leave any non-lowercase-letter characters unchanged.
problems.hint: For each character, check if it's a lowercase letter. If so, shift it using its position in the alphabet and wrap around with the modulo operator (`% 26`).

problems.title: Basic Class: Dog
problems.prompt: Complete the `Dog` class so that `Dog(name)` creates a dog with that name, and `.bark()` returns the string `"{name} says Woof!"` (e.g. `"Rex says Woof!"`).
problems.hint: In `__init__`, save `name` as `self.name`. In `bark`, use an f-string like `f"{self.name} says Woof!"`.

problems.title: Rectangle Class
problems.prompt: Complete the `Rectangle` class: `Rectangle(width, height)` stores both, `.area()` returns `width * height`, and `.perimeter()` returns `2 * (width + height)`.
problems.hint: Store `width` and `height` as `self.width` / `self.height` in `__init__`, then use them in `area` and `perimeter`.

problems.title: Inheritance: Animal Sounds
problems.prompt: The `Animal` base class has a `speak()` method that returns `"..."`. Complete `Dog` and `Cat`, which inherit from `Animal` and override `speak()` to return `"Woof!"` and `"Meow!"` respectively.
problems.hint: Overriding just means writing a new `speak` method in the subclass — it doesn't need to call the parent's version.

problems.title: Static Variable: Counter
problems.prompt: Complete the `Counter` class so that every time a new `Counter()` is created, the class variable `count` increases by 1. Add a method `get_count()` that returns the current value of `count`.
problems.hint: In `__init__`, increase the class variable with `Counter.count += 1` (not `self.count`, which would create a separate instance variable).

problems.title: Bank Account
problems.prompt: Complete the `BankAccount` class: `BankAccount(balance)` stores the starting balance. `.deposit(amount)` adds to the balance. `.withdraw(amount)` subtracts from the balance, but does nothing if `amount` is greater than the current balance. `.balance` should always reflect the current balance.
problems.hint: Store `balance` as `self.balance`. In `withdraw`, check `if amount <= self.balance` before subtracting.

problems.title: Student Average
problems.prompt: Complete the `Student` class: `Student(name)` stores the name and starts with an empty list of grades. `.add_grade(score)` adds a score to the list. `.average()` returns the average of all grades as a float (return `0.0` if there are no grades).
problems.hint: Store an empty list in `__init__`. `add_grade` appends to it. `average` divides the sum of the list by its length — but check for an empty list first to avoid dividing by zero.

problems.title: Inheritance with super(): Vehicle
problems.prompt: Complete the `Vehicle` base class: `Vehicle(wheels)` stores the number of wheels. Then complete `Car`, which inherits from `Vehicle`. `Car(brand)` should call `Vehicle.__init__` with `4` wheels (using `super()`) and also store `brand`. Add a method `describe()` on `Car` that returns `"{brand} car with {wheels} wheels"`.
problems.hint: Inside `Car.__init__`, call `super().__init__(4)` first, then set `self.brand = brand`.

problems.title: Point Distance
problems.prompt: Complete the `Point` class: `Point(x, y)` stores the coordinates. Add a method `distance_to(other)` that returns the Euclidean distance between `self` and `other` (another `Point`). (`import math` is available for `math.sqrt`.)
problems.hint: The distance formula is `math.sqrt((x2 - x1)**2 + (y2 - y1)**2)` — use `self.x`/`self.y` and `other.x`/`other.y`.
